answer: Resource Inlet Saturation. Each identity must consume a scarce, metered resource inlet (compute quota, bandwidth slot) tied to a physical jetty port; a new identity can only register from an unclaimed port, and ports are capped per region. Duplicates cluster on the same physical shale substrate and expose identical inlet timing signatures. An attacker cloning identities must provision distinct physical ports and quota, paying full hardware and subscription cost per clone rather than marginal software cost.
